note: MPI-443 made npm test + npm run test:desktop a release gate, but the gate is a human step in mpi-version-bump - nothing runs the suites on push. A windows-latest runner can run BOTH today: Electron needs no xvfb on Windows, and Playwright drives it through the electron npm binary, so no npx playwright install step is needed. The one blocker is real and must be decided first: package.json line 28 pins "@cubric/connector": "file:../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector", a sibling path that does not exist on a lone checkout, so npm ci fails before any test runs. Three ways out, all needing a call from the user: (a) a second actions/checkout of the private MadPonyInteractive/Cubric-Studio repo with a PAT secret, (b) publish @cubric/connector to a registry, (c) vendor it into this repo. Note the existing .github/workflows/build-portable.yml runs NO tests - it only dispatches the private mpi-ci build on a v* tag, so a red suite currently cannot stop a build.

Investigated the three options and found a fourth that beats all of them. dist/ is untracked in Cubric-Studio so a private checkout would also need a tsc build; vendoring would fork an interop contract against the documented ownership split. But all three consumers already dynamic-import the SDK inside try/catch and handle its absence by design (brokerBoot.js returns null with an SDK-not-installed comment), so it is an OPTIONAL dependency declared as a hard one. Moving it out of dependencies unblocks npm ci with no secret, no registry and no copy, and may also fix the shipped macOS dangling-symlink bug on MPI-416. Needs testing on a repo copy before committing - a missing file: target may still break lockfile resolution even under optionalDependencies.
